newsitem.title: USA: Boston Ed, atty genl OK deregulation deal.
newsitem.headline: Boston Ed, atty genl OK deregulation deal.

text.p: Boston Edison reached a deal with Massachusetts state officials late Wednesday that would let its 661,000 customers choose another utility and guarantee an initial 10 percent rate cut to those who stay.

The accord, which must be approved by the state's Department of Public Utilities, is the third negotiated by Attorney General Scott Harshbarger and officials from Gov. William Weld's office. Massachusetts Electric, a subsidiary of New England Electric System, and Eastern Edison Co, a subsidiary of Eastern Utilties, have similar deals.
Talks with other utilities are continuing, Harshbarger's spokesman said Thursday.
The agreements, which cover 1.8 million or two-thirds of the state's utility customers, would let consumers start buying their electricity from another supplier starting Jan 1.
For those who do not chose another utility, Boston Ed agreed to offer an inital rate cut of 10 percent. The so-called standard offer would be 10.7 cents per kilowatt hour, down from the current 11.9.
